title: Constitution built-in document type: shape rules enforced by lore check, singleton, template (OPAG-425 R1, R2, R3, R4, R9)
description: Binding record: opum-doc main 7831fff, docs/adr/add-constitution-and-constants-document-types-to-lore.md. Add built-in type Constitution (slug constitution) per R1: a lore-only change, no OKF spec change; if the OKF 0.1 legacy-six-type freeze is load-bearing, argue it to opum-agent with the reason rather than exempting silently. R2: at most one per bundle, checked by lore check (new singleton logic). R3: its rules run in lore check, not only lore validate (a second call site beside check's per-file type peek, check.ts ~478-490). R4 shape: frontmatter version (SemVer), ratified and last_amended (ISO, last_amended >= ratified), amendment_authority; required sections Principles, Governance, Amendment log; optional Constraints, Quality gates, Exceptions; each principle a level-3 heading 'P<n>. <Name>', stable id never reused, with at least one uppercase RFC 2119/8174 keyword, a 'Rationale:' and a 'Check:'; the Amendment log's top row matches version and last_amended; no unresolved template placeholders; a WARNING above 150 lines in Principles. R9: 'lore new constitution' template with RFC 8174 boilerplate, one example principle with MUST/Rationale/Check, a Governance section naming agent-drafted, human-ratified amendment by PR linked to an ADR, the Amendment log, and a comment recommending CODEOWNERS required review (lore cannot enforce who edits, and says so).

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore check fails a Constitution missing each required section or field, a principle without a keyword, Rationale or Check, an Amendment log whose top row disagrees with version/last_amended, an unresolved placeholder, and a second Constitution in the bundle; it warns above 150 Principles lines; each proven by a test
lore new constitution produces a document that lore check passes, and a test proves a valid Constitution passes
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

plan: 1. Add built-in Constitution (slug constitution) to the story-convention profile: required string fields version, ratified, last_amended, amendment_authority; required sections Principles, Governance, Amendment log (R1, R4 declarative half).

2. New core module src/core/type-rules.ts: a registry keyed by canonical type name carrying content rules, a singleton flag, and lore new seeds. Constitution registers: SemVer version, ISO ratified/last_amended with last_amended >= ratified, principles as ### P<n>. <Name> with unique ids, an uppercase RFC 2119/8174 keyword, Rationale: and Check:, Amendment log top row = version/last_amended, no unresolved placeholders, warning above 150 Principles lines (R4).

3. Wire content rules into lore validate (validateConceptText) and, as the second call site, into lore check beside the per-file type peek in src/commands/check.ts tryConceptsForBundle, which also counts singleton types per bundle and errors on the second (R2, R3). Generic by type so LCLI-596 registers Constants as one entry.

4. Built-in Constitution template for lore new constitution: RFC 8174 boilerplate, example principle with MUST/Rationale/Check, Governance naming agent-drafted human-ratified amendment by PR linked to an ADR, Amendment log, CODEOWNERS comment stating lore cannot enforce who edits (R9).
5. Tests: one per AC1 failure mode, a valid Constitution passes, lore new constitution output passes lore check; mutation-test the singleton check.
6. Regenerate committed .lore/schemas via bun run lore schema export from source; gates: full bun test and bun run lore check exit 0.
implementationNotes: Binding record read by ref: opum-doc docs/adr/add-constitution-and-constants-document-types-to-lore.md at 7831fff; the copy on opum-doc main is byte-identical (last commit touching it 6e1de57, ODOC-283), so no later amendment applies. The ADR's cited check.ts:478-490 was read against main 3ef3125; on this dev the per-file type peek is tryConceptsForBundle in src/commands/check.ts, which is where the second call site went.

R1 OKF 0.1 question, NOT settled here and flagged for opum-agent: Constitution is declared on BOTH the 0.2 and the 0.1 built-in profile, per R1's literal 'available on every OKF version lore supports'. Evidence: the freeze's own documented reason (okf-conformance.md: 'Under 0.1, the new 0.2 families retain their prior extension treatment') is scoped to OKF 0.2 SPEC types; Constitution is in no OKF spec. Measured by ref on dev and main, 20 of 20 root indexes read: opum-agent, opum-doc, lore-cli, quest-cli, lore-web, quest-web declare okf_version 0.1; opum-cli-e2e, opum-web, opum-marketplace, opum-fleet declare 0.2. Exempting 0.1 would leave type Constitution an unknown type (no shape rules) in 6 of 10 repos, including opum-agent, where OPAG-423's constitution is expected to land. Reversing is one line in storyConventionProfile plus the test 'the built-in OKF 0.1 consumer profile omits the OKF 0.2 spec type but keeps lore-only Constitution'.

Shape for LCLI-596: src/core/type-rules.ts holds a registry keyed by canonical type name; each entry has check (content rules), singleton (bool), and seed (lore new frontmatter plus body vars). Neither call site names a type: validateConceptText runs entry.check, and commands/check.ts tryConceptsForBundle (beside the per-file type peek) runs validate's full per-file judgement for any registered type (errors plus type-shape findings, reported under rule type-shape), then collects singleton candidates and calls singletonFindings once per bundle (rule singleton-type). template.ts buildNewConcept applies entry.seed. Constants is one more TYPE_RULES entry plus a profile type and a BUILTIN_TEMPLATES entry. Rules apply only when the ACTIVE profile declares the type (a custom profile replaces the built-in vocabulary).

R4 interpretations, each named so it can be argued: (a) the Amendment log is a pipe table with Version and Date header columns, newest row first; lore parses CommonMark with no GFM extension, so the table is read from the paragraph's raw source instead of adding a markdown dependency. (b) An unresolved placeholder is lore's {{name}} token or Spec Kit's [UPPER_SNAKE] bracket token (underscore required, so [RFC2119] is not one), in frontmatter strings and body prose, excluding code spans, code blocks and HTML comments. (c) An empty Principles section is an error. (d) Never-reused is enforced within one document (a duplicate P<n> is an error); reuse across revisions needs commit history, the same reason the ADR defers version-bump consistency. (e) Keywords count only outside code spans; Rationale: and Check: match at the start of any paragraph line, including list items and bold labels.

Consequences found, outside this task's scope and not fixed here: (1) Declaring version/ratified/last_amended/amendment_authority adds them to the profile-wide canonicalKeyOrder, placed with the other per-type fields (the compiler's general rule, as for Arc's tasks/specs). A document of ANY type already using one of those names as an extension key is reordered on its next lore rewrite (ADR-0011). Measured 0 of 82 lore-cli docs carry any of the four, with a positive control; fleet exposure unmeasured. (2) lore new constitution writes ratified/last_amended unquoted, and lore validate's quote-safety lint then warns twice on its own output (YAML 1.1 reads a bare date as a date). lore check, including --strict, is clean because check does not report quote-safety warnings. Quoting bare dates is a serializer change under ADR-0011 byte stability, so it needs its own task; the warning is pinned in test/constitution.test.ts so it cannot change unnoticed. (3) profileDigest changed: lore-cli's own lore check exited 6 on schema drift before re-export (the R10 rollout effect), and bun run lore schema export rewrote 8 digest stamps and added constitution.schema.json.

Evidence, local, lore 0.9.3 from source (bun run src/cli.ts) and quest 0.10.0: full bun test exit 0 (3521 pass, 0 fail, 3522 ran); bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings); bunx tsc --noEmit exit 0; biome reports 0 errors (3 warnings and 1 info, all in files this task did not touch). test/constitution.test.ts: 34 tests, one per AC1 failure mode (4 missing fields, 3 missing sections, SemVer, ISO date, last_amended before ratified, missing keyword, keyword only in code, missing Rationale, missing Check, bad heading, reused id, no principle, Amendment log version and date mismatch, no table, both placeholder forms, second Constitution, >150-line warning) plus a valid Constitution passing check --strict and validate, 0.1 enforcement, custom-profile exemption, and lore new constitution output passing check --strict. Mutation: with the singletonFindings call removed from commands/check.ts, the full suite went red on exactly the 2 predicted tests ('a second Constitution fails lore check, naming the first' and 'a second lore new constitution is caught by check's singleton rule'), 3519 others green; restored, all green. CI not yet run.

Orchestrator rulings for the #296 amendment (recorded on opum-agent OPAG-425, relayed by the coordinator; the counts below were measured by the reviewer by ref, with controls, and are relayed here, not re-resolved by this session). OKF 0.1: Constitution stays on BOTH 0.1 and 0.2, as built. (a) New types must not change how an existing doc of another type is written; the reviewer measured 0 of 384 fleet docs carrying version, ratified, last_amended or amendment_authority in frontmatter, so the global canonical key order STAYS as built, the zero being the ruling's exception. (b) A fresh lore new constitution must pass lore validate --strict with zero warnings: the existing quoteLeadingZeroStrings dump transform in src/core/concept.ts now also double-quotes a string matching ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$ (ADR-0011 section 4 minimal YAML-safe quoting); the reviewer measured 0 of 384 fleet docs with an unquoted bare-date frontmatter value, so no existing fleet doc is rewritten differently.

Ruling A on review finding 2 (orchestrator, recorded on opum-agent OPAG-425): the built-in Constitution rules (content rules, singleton, SemVer, dates, Amendment log, placeholders, lore new seed) attach ONLY when the type resolves to lore's BUILT-IN declaration. A profile.toml that redeclares Constitution opts out entirely and keeps its own fields and sections, exactly as before this PR; adding a built-in type must never change behaviour for a bundle that already defined a same-named type. Implemented generically in typeRuleFor via profile.ts isBuiltinTypeDeclaration (object identity with the built-in profile's compiled type on either OKF version), so Constants (LCLI-596) inherits it. Tested with a custom Constitution aliased Charter with sections [Articles]: two type: Charter docs pass lore check --strict with no finding, the custom section is still enforced, and a control proves the built-in still gets every rule. Info, left as is: the singleton is counted per selected bundle root (lore check a b counts each root separately).

Review findings fixed on #296 (reviewer read head 976140eb). 1: docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh LCLI-299 AC3 count 8 to 9 plus constitution.schema.json in the sorted list, and constitution added to the four per-type loops (1383, 1434, 1441 teardown, 1616); CI run 36265508880 had 383 passed, 2 failed (AC3 and the AC4 teardown), so the prediction is 388 passed, 0 failed (+2 fixed, +3 new loop checks). 4: paragraphLines treats an mdast break as a line break. 5: firstPipeTable finds a table whose header sits under prose lines in the same paragraph (GFM interrupt), matching header and delimiter cell counts. 6: proseText, paragraphLines and frontmatterStrings use explicit stacks; 20,000 nested blockquotes are tested in validate and check. 7: cells are read as rendered inline text (bold, emphasis, code); code spans become an opaque token so a label inside code does not count but Check: with code content does; link, image and definition URLs and titles are scanned for {{x}}; the Spec Kit form is now two or more _-joined upper-case segments whose first and last are letters only, not followed by [ or (, so [RFC_2119], [ISO_8601], [RFC2119] and reference links do not match. 8: check keeps validate's own rule names (frontmatter, required-section) for profile-shape errors, type-shape only for the type's content rules, and no longer reports quote-safety for a Constitution.

Amendment evidence, local, lore from source and quest 0.10.0, after merging origin/dev (clean, no docker/ overlap): full bun test exit 0 (3603 pass, 0 fail, 3604 ran); bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings); tsc exit 0; biome 0 errors.
